title: What to do about BF bound to dated trim in 80s rancher | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "ladybeanofbunny", "author_name": "ladybeanofbunny", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/ladybeanofbunny", "date": "2024-12-01", "text": "We've already tackled if you renovation projects together here since I moved in with him 9 years ago. The house was already project in progress when I came along so a lot of the first decisions about design and decorating had nothing to do with me.Moving on... about the house:This is a 1980s fairly prefab rancher and looking at photos of the house when he first bought it and the way it was decorated, all I can say is 1987 called and they want their house back!!!The house was plagued with stained hollow door doors (bifold no less for the closets) and awful white loopy pile wall to wall carpeting which of this the last room remaining with it is it the living room I just hope we're about to embark on now. The living room kitchen and dining room are the final pieces in the upcoming year.Here's my problem, ok? I have much reverence for old homes and original woodwork- stained, NOT painted over.BUT in my mind the wood trim used around the windows doors and floor in this house were just regular old cheap pine trim. Granted it's still very expensive but as he embarked in renovating this house in the beginning (before me) he opted to refresh the stain on all the wood trim AND matched the wood flooring he replaced the carpeting with the stupid prefab 80s trim he saved as if it's a special feature of the house.His choice was certainly not what I would have picked. A very orangey reddish wide \"spiced maple\" that has a very rustic look but uniform and milled enough in a way to be too perfect to really have any true rustic feel.Moving forward, as I joined forces and started planning redoing a spare bedroom into a spa inspired relaxation room- the wood trim just didn't fit any aesthetic I was going for but he made it clear I was not painting the trim. Oh did I mention he also replaced all the cheap hollow core doors with solid four -panel wood doors that he spent months staining? In fact when we first met when we used to chat on work nights this was often what he said he was doing. So the house has matching solid wood stained doors now that were NOT cheap to match the 80s pine trim. In the end I opted for mounting ceiling to floor length white sheers over the windows in my spa room just to hide the windows with the wood trim and give the room a brighter fresher look.The last piece of the puzzle is a massive renovation which involves the living room dining room and kitchen. We've hired an architect to help with the project because we have a lot of design dilemmas and we haven't been able to figure out ourselves and it'll probably involve substantial total redesign of the space, possibly a new roofline and/or addition.I've never been more frustrated by the stupid wood trim then I am now - since we are locked into decorating around it to match, throughout the entire house!He's a bit older than me and in my opinion a little too matchy matchy and locked into fairly conventional somewhat outdated design concepts whereas I've seen lots of different styles of design. I went to aet school and in my early adolescent years (8th grade-11th) my plan was actually to become an interior designer before opting for fashion.My tastes have always been less traditional and now at current age many years later after traveling and accumulating experience and exposure to different places I've cultivated and developed a fondness for very elegant, elevated modern style. I've even acquired a strong inclination towards mid-century modern which contrasts so incredibly with my earlier dead-set fixation with 19th and early 20th century style.That being said... this house is very interesting. It has very interesting roofline and the property also has a very multi leveled interesting landscape that we're working to design around.I've been drawn a lot to mid-century modern architecture and realized it's the variation in roofline and tall windows and such that speaks to me. This house is basically, for a lack of a better word, a blank canvas. It is a 1980s rancher with similar qualities to a mid-century home.The living room has a fabulous slanted ceiling with a peak of 12'. However there's a wall between the LR and adjacent tiny kitchen and dining room that are basically built into a little box under a flat 8' ceiling. I've already told him we have to open the ceiling on the front of the house, too, remove the wall and create a large airy open floor space. I usually prefer a formal dining room but in this house it doesn't work.I've been looking a lot at different elements of modern design (whatever of the thousand's of styles they might be called) and he often shoots me down on the basis of not \"going with the house\" and is very frustrating. So you're saying you want a late 1980s traditional home?? I mean... What exactly are you fighting to maintain consistency with here?? (Putting aside for a second the rustic wide planked wood floors that do not match the period the house lol...)The other problem is that we live in the woods so he thinks the house through and through needs to match the landscape. Everything has to be natural colours.As we embark on this project I'm exceedingly concerned about his attachment to the windows doors and trim he won't deviate from because carrying this over into whatever kitchen dining room and living room design we choose- it's going to greatly impact the final look.I literally haven't been able to find a single kitchen style that looks nice that has stained wood trim windows like we have and especially if we bump out the house, any new windows and doors will be more of what's in the rest of the house greatly limiting what we can and cannot do and look good.I'm not sure there is any way to ever convince him that perhaps we can have something different. Unless the architect offers a good enough argument and he listens.Literally everything I see online when I Google this is about HOW to paint wood trim, etc. Not a single modern kitchen has the traditional stained windows and doors like we have. Maybe if it's a farmhouse kitchen they have very rustic plain wood but not like what we have.Too many rules. Way too many. A little abandonment from the traditional would do both he and this very uncreative boring house a world of good.To recap.... everything on the side of the house after the living room dining room and kitchen has already been finished with matching stained window, door and floor trim. main_question: {"author_id": "nancyjane-gardener", "author_name": "nancyjane_gardener", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/nancyjane-gardener", "date": "2024-12-01", "text": "I was reading an article on leaving leaves. other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "laceyvail", "author_name": "laceyvail 6A, WV", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/laceyvail", "date": "2024-12-21", "text": "When I started my veggie garden 3 years ago, I was appalled the find the soil the worst clay I've ever seen.  I garden in permanent beds, not raised, with wood mulched paths in between.  The first fall I piled leaves, picked up from friends' yards, on the beds, add some non peat based compost, and covered all with hay that didn't have weed seed.  The following season, when I peeled back the hay, I chopped in the leaves with a Korean hand hoe and sowed seed..  Plants I just popped into the ground surrounded by the hay and leaves underneath.  Of course I was also using organic fertilizers--Coast of Maine and Espoma products.  Also, when a crop was finished, say lettuce, I chopped it up in place and added more hay.  For bulkier crops, like cabbage, I added the green side leaves to the beds under the hay.  I had no access to manure. Now, at the end of the third year, the soil is hugely improved.  My worst problem now are the moles, all eating the earthworms after they exploded with all the goodies now available to them.", "images": []}}

title: Wrestling with the jungle | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "melissaaipapa", "author_name": "Melissa Northern Italy zone 8", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/melissaaipapa", "date": "2024-12-04", "text": "During a day of various kinds of piddling around, one chore was getting the worst of the wisteria out of the persimmon in front of the house.  The wisteria has the pergola to climb on, but naturally it wants to expand its power base.  It got cut back hard--massacred--about two and a half years ago when we had the foundation work done and a new pergola installed, and then afterwards I didn't prune it much for a year or two.  Well, it's back. The persimmon, meanwhile, gets a little bigger every year.  It was a sapling when we bought the property; now it's a tree, reaching this year to the power line that runs to the top of our three story house.  It too grows over the pergola, leaning on it like a kind of horizontal espaliering:  this makes it harder to keep the wisteria out of it, but I like the effect.  I'm not sure, giving the density of all the plants competing for space, that it makes the persimmons themselves easier to reach as I would like. The last major member of the plant community striving to take over the pergola is 'Archduke Joseph'.  It started out about twenty years ago as a miniscule cutting grown plant.  Then it grew, as did the persimmon.  Then I had to decide what to do when the persimmon started to shade out the growing rose. Both by that time were too large to move. I wasn't too hopeful about this, but I tied canes of 'Archduke Joseph' through the persimmon, and from that point both grew together, getting larger every year.  I'm not sure the persimmon likes the competition, but both survive, grow, and flower/fruit, so all is more or less well.  'Archduke Joseph' grows through and over the persimmon as well as onto the pergola:  the top of its growth is somewhat above my eye level as I look out from my first floor (above ground floor) bedroom window.  It's trying right now to bloom, but I think doesn't have enough light and warmth to open its many buds.  I estimate it to be about eighteen feet tall, with a considerable spread.", "images": []}

title: Early English Roses That Are Still Blooming In December | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "rick-sauder", "author_name": "Rideau Rose Lad", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/rick-sauder", "date": "2024-12-04", "text": "It is a cool December day in the South Okanagan.  The ridges surrounding the valley lakes are all cloaked in snow.  The snow level is about 500 meters, the valley bottom at about 150 meters.  It has snowed lower down in the past week, but grudgingly melted thereafter.  Today I decided to go for a walk, so I made the trip to my volunteer garden in Summerland.  Lots of paths and trails, meandering garden paths, a trail along the deep and impressive Trout Creek canyon.  Not another soul there.  Just a lovely place to wander on an overcast early winters day.  Of course, I checked on the roses for which I am responsible.  Many are migrants from California, as you may know.  But it is still surprising to see how many buds they sport and how hard some of them want to bloom.   Bibi Maizoon (the name is a link) - This is a very rare old Austin rose, we have three plants in the garden.  The cultivar was released in 1989 and is a cross between \"The Reeve\" and Chaucer.  She is now planted next to a very young plant of The Reeve, which I hope will come into its own next summer. To tell you the truth, Bibi it has not impressed me much until now.  I dug up and moved a very ancient plant last spring while extending a pathway.  She has been blooming a lot since September.  Her old compatriots which were not moved, bloom in one or two flushes over summer.  Neither of those plants has done anything for months.  But the one I moved has been blooming frequently with very deep pink globular cupped blooms that I like very much.  In addition, while many other varieties are still trying to push out blooms, they mostly fail to open, or are ruined.  Not Bibi, she seems to like the cool fall and winter weather.  This plant very much seems to have benefitted from her move and has a new blooming attitude.   Saint Cecilia (link) -  I have two plants of this rose from the final batch of cuttings imported from John's rose garden in Riverside Califonia two summers ago.  They are both one year old plants, small but established and raring to go.  I grew St. Cecelia in my Ontario Garden and whe was wonderful.  A good bloomer, upright habit with lovely cupped blooms and potent fragrance.  Released in 1987, this one has \"Wife of Bath\" on both sides.  She is also and extremely cold hardy cultivar, zone 4b in my Ontario garden.  Now she is showing a willingness to produce lovely blooms at the freezing mark.  What's not to like?   Ambridge Rose (link) -  I have two plants of Ambridge Rose in the Gardens, the mother plant and a second year cutting grown plant.  The mother plant too was moved last sping and has also decide to show some pizazz in her new location.  This cultivar was released in 1990, result of a cross between Charles Austin and an unnamed seeding.  She has been blooming well all summer and seems to have gone into overdrive this fall.  Lots of new buds, and impressively, they are opening with a deep Salmon pink colour.  Another older English Rose that is a classic. I am so fortunate to now have responsibility for such a heritage collection of roses . I no longer lust for new cultivars, I evaluate and enjoy the old ones.  They become a bit like old friends. main_question: {"author_id": "tcufrog", "author_name": "tcufrog", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/tcufrog", "date": "2024-12-05", "text": "My mother-in-law lives with us and is getting older. I met with my contractor today who has done amazing work remodelling our kitchen, our master bath and another bathroom upstairs that had to be gutted due to mold and water damage. He has built ADA compliant bathrooms and is very thorough and meticulous.  I want to do my own research though and was wondering if anyone knew of a good online guide.  I'd  love to hear about fellow Houzzers' experience with using and designing an accessible home bathroom. We met today and I gave him my spec sheet for the project.  He measured the room and will meet with his tiler to discuss the dimensions the shower needs to make it curbless.  His tiler did a curbless shower in our main bathroom and did an excellent job. One thing my contractor suggested that I'm iffy on is installing a pedestal sink instead.  The bathroom is quite long but not very wide.  He thought it might be easier for my mother-in-law to use a pedestal sink instead of a cabinet sink if she's in a wheelchair at some point.  Thoughts?", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "kendrahhendra", "author_name": "Kendrah", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/kendrahhendra", "date": "2024-12-05", "text": "We have a studio apartment down the hall from our main apartment and wanted to make it a comfortable and safe place for my aging parents to spend lengthy amounts of time in and live in if ever needed.  I learned a ton a long the way from my father (an engineer who did lots of public building design including ADA), an OT we hired who specializes in aging in place home design, and from reading a ton online. * ADA requirements are not actually what you want to use in a home.  (Dad + OT agreed.) ADA standards are made for the general public and are created to accommodate the average person.  Your home should be made to accommodate your loved one.  Have your mother-in-law reach out and see where *her* arm goes to grab for stability, balance, and coming to standing.  Base things on *her* height.  I had my mom and dad test a lot of arm reaches and positions to see what would be comfortable for *them* to grab. * Only 7% of older adults become wheelchair bound.  Is there something in particular that indicates that your mother-in-law is going to be destined for a wheelchair?  If not, the much more important things to focus on are: 1. Balance and stability - as those are issues that so many adults have - a long countertop is useful for this, not having to step to different locations to reach for cosmetics, toiletries, being able to set things on a counter if an action needs to gets broken down into many parts.  Yes, a short sink is helpful if she is in a wheelchair but if she is the other 93% of the population, having a taller sink is better so she doesn't have to bend down so far to use it. 2. How to move around the space with two people in it - if she ever needs assistance with grooming or on the toilet - I'd never put pony walls on two sides of a toilet as you then cannot stand by her side if she needs help.  Have a grab bar on one side.  If she ends up needing one on the second side, install one that can hinge up and down from the wall as needed. 3. Reducing fall risks - Make sure floor surfaces have a high anti-slip rating - don't just rely on the adage that grout on mosaic tile will do enough to reduce slipping; Don't use grab bars that double as towel rods - cause of lots of accidents, use grab bars for balance and hooks for towels; Make a very good lighting design so there are no shadows, the room is well lit, it is easy and logical where to turn on the lights (remember no electric and plumbing in a pocket door wall); add plenty of outlets so you don't have to move around the room a lot to plug something in; have a place to sit down and dry off. 4. Make open floor space for a walker to live while she is on the toilet or in the shower.  (Twice as many people use walkers as use wheelchairs and way more than that use canes.) Wonderful that you are doing this.  I cared for my father-in-law for many years and loved him as I do my own father.  I get it!  He had dementia and needs so much help but was never in a wheelchair.  Went from walking to bed bound.  Same was with my two uncles with parkinsons, walking to bedbound.  My grandmother used a wheel chair for two weeks.  We made do without wheelchair accessible accomodations.", "images": []}}

main_question: {"author_id": "publickman", "author_name": "Lars", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/publickman", "date": "2024-12-05", "text": "I've made this coleslaw several times and finally got around to trying to write it down, so that I can remember how to make it.  It is my favorite coleslaw recipe. Napa Cabbage Coleslaw Cut the cabbage leaves in half, stack on top of each other, and slice very thinly with a very sharp chef's knife, preferably Japanese. Put the cabbage in a large glass or plastic bowl and sprinkle with the salt. Mix the salt in thoroughly with a wooden spoon or hands and allow to rest for 20 minutes.  Stir the mixture again and allow to rest 20 additional minutes, and repeat, for a total of one hour resting time. Add water to cabbage to rinse out the brine, squeeze out all water, and repeat so that cabbage is thoroughly rinsed, and let drain in a colander after squeezing out as much water as possible. Put the cabbage back into the bowl and add carrot, onion, bell pepper, and black pepper, and mix thoroughly. Make a dressing with mayonnaise, olive oil, and vinegar, and add to cabbage mixture, stirring to combine.  Adjust the dressing to taste, if needed.  It might need more vinegar, especially if you use rice wine vinegar instead of cider vinegar. Store in an air-tight container in the refrigerator for at least an hour before serving. Options: Use 2 tsp toasted sesame oil instead of olive oil, or add toasted sesame seeds or furikake when serving, for Japanese version. *Note: I made this by adding the mayonnaise first and then added the olive oil and vinegar without mixing the dressing because I did not have any vinegar in the house at the time. title: Senior citizen stuck in wrong house in difficult real estate market | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "treadsoftly", "author_name": "treadsoftly", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/treadsoftly", "date": "2024-12-08", "text": "I loved my house when I bought it 30 years ago. But conditions have changed and it's no longer working for me. It will work less and less as I age. The main issues: None of those was really a problem 30 yeas ago. I finally decided to move. The selection of available houses in my area is extremely small. In one year of daily searching I only found four houses worth visiting. Plan B is to build a new house, so I started looking for land, only to discover that there is even less desirable land than houses. If I could add another $100,000 to my house-buying budget, yes, I could find a house to buy. But that would be an over-investment in a too-large home when I want to downsize. Some positives in my situation: I'm still strong and reasonably healthy. I own my home mortgage free. I have enough cash to buy land. My house would sell quickly, and the sale of the house should cover the cost to buy or build a small house. I have a good realtor and a general contractor lined up to build a new house. I've met with a bank and made a plan to qualify for a short-term loan if needed. I'm still working and also have social security. Despite those positives, I feel like I'm stuck in a real estate market that's not moving. The value of my house has increased steadily over the last five years, but that doesn't help much if there is no suitable land or houses to buy. I considered trying to make my house more livable by addressing some of the things on the above list. Each of those involves numerous difficulties and expense, and it doesn't seem to make sense to put money into the wrong house.  I don't want to live in an apartment, condo, or mobile home. At this point I'm losing heart. I fear having to live in my current house into my 80s and 90s. I don't know what to do at this point. I feel like there must be a solution somewhere, but I'm not seeing it. My question: Is there anything more I can do at this point to improve my housing situation?", "images": []}

We won't live forever and chances are we will need some help as we get older -- what's the plan for that?  Have you spoken to a financial advisor about your future? What does your family think? There is no law that requires you to purchase another house when you sell your current home.  You can invest the proceeds of the sale and use it to cover rent in a nice home for a long time.  Or you can invest in a senior living community where you can live the rest of your life. Or you can buy a small condo with less upkeep and you can travel as much as you like without worry. title: Overwintering Temperate Shrubs | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "anamandy", "author_name": "lovetogarden", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/anamandy", "date": "2024-12-09", "text": "I have a few potted shrubs that are more suited to a warmer climate than mine (dwarf hydrangeas, fig, and French tarragon), and read that they can be overwintered in a garage or shed. Since these go dormant and send up new shoots in the spring, do they have to receive sunlight? Both my garage and shed do not get any natural light. So, can they be overwintered in the dark? Also, how often will I need to water them, if at all?", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "gardengal48", "author_name": "gardengal48 (PNW Z8/9)", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/gardengal48", "date": "2024-12-09", "text": "As the plants are in dormancy and lack leaves in winter, they have no ability or need to photosynthesize so require no light. Provide only enough water to keep the soil barely damp.....lack of leaves also means they don't transpire much either.", "images": []}, "Comment 2": {"author_id": "luis-pr", "author_name": "luis_pr", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/luis-pr", "date": "2024-12-09", "text": "\"do they have to receive sunlight?\" No, not until the spring. \"can they be overwintered in the dark?\" Yes, you can overwinter either in a basement, a shed or a garage. \"how often will I need to water them, if at all?\" That depends on your winters, shrub size, pot size, etc. In some locations, they lose humidity faster than in others so test the soil moisture and water if it feels dry. You may not be able to insert a finger through the soil if the soil has frozen though.   Consider wrapping the pot with insulating materials like burlap to help retain warmth. But generally speaking, it may be more practical to wait to water until temps are above freezing or until the soil thaws. I typically water about monthly in my garage, maybe a cup of water, but it may require more/less in your place. main_question: {"author_id": "ei-laurence-levy-studio-votre-decoratrice-pfvwfr-pf~1293701073", "author_name": "EI- Laurence LEVY (STUDIO VOTRE DECORATRICE)", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/interior-architects/ei-laurence-levy-studio-votre-decoratrice-pfvwfr-pf~1293701073", "date": "2024-12-09", "text": "Cher.s propri\u00e9taires \ud83d\ude0a, En tant qu\u2019architecte d\u2019int\u00e9rieur, j\u2019ai accompagn\u00e9 de nombreux particuliers dans leur projet de construction ou de r\u00e9novation. Que vous envisagiez d\u2019acheter une maison ou de construire la v\u00f4tre, il est essentiel de bien pr\u00e9parer chaque \u00e9tape pour \u00e9viter les mauvaises surprises. Voici mes conseils pour aborder sereinement votre projet.   1 - IDENTIFIER LES BESOINS DES LA PREMIERE VISITE Tirer partie du changement de propri\u00e9taire Les anciens occupants, par habitude ou par manque de besoin, n\u2019ont pas toujours entrepris les travaux n\u00e9cessaires. Le changement de propri\u00e9taire constitue une opportunit\u00e9 id\u00e9ale pour repenser le potentiel du lieu. Tout comme un v\u00e9hicule d\u2019occasion pass\u00e9 par un contr\u00f4le avant de changer de main, une maison m\u00e9rite une analyse approfondie pour identifier les travaux n\u00e9cessaires. D\u00e9finir les solutions possibles Apr\u00e8s avoir rep\u00e9r\u00e9 les points \u00e0 am\u00e9liorer lors des visites, il est temps d\u2019identifier les solutions adapt\u00e9es. Qu\u2019il s\u2019agisse de travaux de mise aux normes, d\u2019optimisation des espaces ou d\u2019am\u00e9liorations esth\u00e9tiques, cette \u00e9tape est cruciale pour l\u2019\u00e9laboration de la pertinence de votre projet. En sollicitant desdevis d\u00e9taill\u00e9s pour chaque intervention envisag\u00e9e, vous pourrez \u00e9tablir un budget global comprenant l\u2019achat et les travaux. Planifiez votre projet avec soin Selon l\u2019ampleur des travaux \u00e0 r\u00e9aliser, il faudra organiser un planning pr\u00e9cis. Cette planification vous permettra de coordonner les diff\u00e9rentes \u00e9tapes du chantier et d\u2019anticiper votre emm\u00e9nagement tant attendu. S\u2019il s\u2019agit d\u2019une r\u00e9novation majeure, pr\u00e9voir des p\u00e9riodes transitoires o\u00f9 le logement ne sera pas habitable peut \u00e9galement \u00eatre n\u00e9cessaire. En r\u00e9sum\u00e9, r\u00e9ussir son projet de maison, qu\u2019il s\u2019agisse d\u2019une construction ou d\u2019une r\u00e9novation, exige une pr\u00e9paration rigoureuse. Analysez le bien, \u00e9valuez les travaux n\u00e9cessaires, obtenez des devis pr\u00e9cis et planifiez chaque \u00e9tape. Vous pourrez ainsi entrer dans votre nouvelle maison en toute s\u00e9r\u00e9nit\u00e9, en profitant d\u2019un espace parfaitement adapt\u00e9 \u00e0 vos envies et besoins.   Cr\u00e9dits photo Laurence Levy \u2013 R\u00e9novation de la fa\u00e7ade, am\u00e9nagement outdoor 2 - LA PLANIFICATION Une fois les travaux identifi\u00e9s et budg\u00e9tis\u00e9s, l\u2019\u00e9tape suivante consiste \u00e0 \u00e9tablir une planification d\u00e9taill\u00e9e. Cette planification est essentielle pour regrouper les interventions des diff\u00e9rents professionnels (ma\u00e7ons, plombiers, \u00e9lectriciens, d\u00e9corateurs, etc.) et pour consid\u00e9rer la dur\u00e9e totale des travaux. Voici les principaux aspects \u00e0 prendre en compte dans votre planification :    Photo non contractuelle Cette organisation m\u00e9thodique vous permettra de profiter de votre maison sans stress et au moment pr\u00e9vu. Une bonne planification est le secret d\u2019un projet r\u00e9ussi, que ce soit pour une r\u00e9novation ou une construction neuve. 3 - LES ASSURANCES : un point souvent n\u00e9glig\u00e9 Pourquoi ces garanties sont cruciales ? Selon l\u2019ampleur des travaux \u00e0 r\u00e9aliser, il faudra organiser un planning pr\u00e9cis. Cette planification vous permettra de coordonner les diff\u00e9rentes \u00e9tapes du chantier et d\u2019anticiper votre emm\u00e9nagement tant attendu. S\u2019il s\u2019agit d\u2019une r\u00e9novation majeure, pr\u00e9voir des p\u00e9riodes transitoires o\u00f9 le logement ne sera pas habitable peut \u00e9galement \u00eatre n\u00e9cessaire. Elles permettent de prot\u00e9ger votre investissement et de limiter les co\u00fbts impr\u00e9vus. Si vous achetez une maison ancienne, n\u2019h\u00e9sitez pas \u00e0 demander les factures et documents relatifs aux travaux r\u00e9cents. Ils seront vos meilleurs alli\u00e9s pour faire valoir vos droits en cas de besoin. Prendre en compte ces \u00e9l\u00e9ments d\u00e8s le d\u00e9part, que ce soit en amont ou en aval des travaux, est essentiel pour s\u00e9curiser votre projet immobilier Assurez-vous de demander tous les justificatifs n\u00e9cessaires avant de finaliser un achat ou de lancer des travaux ! Si un expert valide le d\u00e9sordre, le juge peut condamner le vendeur \u00e0 indemniser l\u2019acheteur. Ce dernier ne pourra pas se d\u00e9rober, quand bien m\u00eame il aurait r\u00e9alis\u00e9 les travaux lui-m\u00eame \u2026 d\u2019o\u00f9 l\u2019int\u00e9r\u00eat pour qui r\u00e9alise ou fait r\u00e9aliser des travaux de les garantir car alors il pourra reporter la charge \u00e0 la compagnie d\u2019assurance (ce qui est syst\u00e9matiquement le cas de travaux r\u00e9alis\u00e9s par des professionnels). En cas de sinistre non couvert par une garantie, le vendeur peut \u00eatre condamn\u00e9 \u00e0 indemniser l\u2019acheteur sur ses fonds propres. Des cas font d\u00e9sormais jurisprudence.   Cr\u00e9dits photo Laurence Levy \u2013 Am\u00e9nagement int\u00e9rieur d\u2019un petit collectif Le second \u0153uvre Vous souhaitez \u00eatre accompagn\u00e9 par notre experte ? il inclut tout ce qui ne rel\u00e8ve pas de la structure principale : plomberie, \u00e9lectricit\u00e9, menuiseries, peintures, etc. Ces \u00e9l\u00e9ments b\u00e9n\u00e9ficient d\u2019une garantie biennale, valable 2 ans apr\u00e8s la fin des travaux. Exemple : une installation \u00e9lectrique remise \u00e0 neuf sera garantie pour une p\u00e9riode de deux ans \u00e0 compter de son ach\u00e8vement. Pour les Travaux r\u00e9cents, qu\u2019ils concernent une maison ancienne ou une construction neuve, les garanties restent identiques :  Ainsi, si vous achetez une maison dont certains travaux ont \u00e9t\u00e9 r\u00e9alis\u00e9s r\u00e9cemment, vous \u00eates en droit de demander r\u00e9paration en cas de sinistre affectant ces \u00e9l\u00e9ments pendant la dur\u00e9e l\u00e9gale de la garantie. 4 - QUE FAIRE EN CAS DE SINISTRE Si un probl\u00e8me survient dans le cadre des garanties : 4 - VOS TRAVAUX FUTURS Si le bien r\u00e9nov\u00e9 devait \u00eatre revendu avant l\u2019extinction des garanties l\u00e9gales selon le type des \u00e9l\u00e9ments concern\u00e9s et tels que d\u00e9crits ci-dessus, le vendeur que sera devenu l\u2019actuel acheteur devra, \u00e0 son tour, les m\u00eames garanties \u00e0 son acheteur du moment \u2026 Nos conseils : demander au vendeur de fournir les factures des travaux et les attestations d\u2019assurance des entreprises ayant r\u00e9alis\u00e9 les travaux. Le notaire qui passera les actes authentiques est d\u2019ailleurs fond\u00e9 \u00e0 demander ces attestations d\u2019assurance.   Cr\u00e9dits photo Laurence Levy \u2013 R\u00e9novation maison ancienne de village en Provence Humidit\u00e9 : Les d\u00e9sordres et pathologies li\u00e9s \u00e0 une gestion inappropri\u00e9e de la teneur en eau des murs, des bois et/ou de l\u2019air, sont parmi les plus nombreux des maux qu\u2019il va falloir traiter, r\u00e9parer ou endiguer. Selon les sympt\u00f4mes relev\u00e9s lors des visites et/ou contr\u00f4les et selon la nature du b\u00e2ti, des actions sont \u00e0 pr\u00e9voir. D\u00e9collement des cr\u00e9pis, salp\u00eatre \u00e0 mi-hauteur de mur : ce sont l\u00e0 des pathologies le plus souvent li\u00e9es \u00e0 une \u00e9tanch\u00e9ification des murs. Il n\u2019y a qu\u2019une seule solution valable : enlever les \u201cgangues\u201d que sont ces cr\u00e9pis et autres \u00e9l\u00e9ments \u00e9tanches. Le mieux est bien s\u00fbr d\u2019en d\u00e9gager les murs sur les 2 faces et sur toute la hauteur. Si, pour des raisons de tenue de l\u2019ouvrage, la chose n\u2019est pas possible, a minima \u201cd\u00e9crouter\u201d la face ext\u00e9rieure sur 1 m\u00e8tre de haut; sur les 2 faces, ce sera mieux. CONCLUSION Soyez \u00e0 la hauteur de votre projet et privil\u00e9giez la r\u00e9flexion sur le type constructif de votre bien. En effet, si nous recherchons en priorit\u00e9 leCONFORT thermiqueet visuel, les diff\u00e9rentes approches de travaux ne sont pas une science exacte surtout en r\u00e9novation du b\u00e2ti ancien. Le r\u00e9sultat en terme de performance dans une maison ancienne ne pourra pas \u00e9galer celle d\u2019une construction neuve, les mat\u00e9riaux n\u2019ayant pas les m\u00eames propri\u00e9t\u00e9s comme l\u2019inertie, la capillarit\u00e9, leur temps de d\u00e9phasage... ___________________________ Laurence LEVY - Architecture int\u00e9rieure & d\u00e9coration des int\u00e9rieurs durables en Provence", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/56720ce70756ee1e_0367-w500-h333-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/fed207b80756ee20_0304-w500-h281-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/2c02013f0756ee20_0305-w500-h333-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/63523ca90756ee21_0307-w500-h281-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/cf6226250756ee23_0307-w500-h281-b0-p0--.jpg"]}

title: My First Experimental Cheesecake--Kiwi Style | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "plllog", "author_name": "plllog", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/plllog", "date": "2024-12-09", "text": "Kiwi style as in using up the kiwi salad which we forgot to serve at Thanksgiving.  I had threatened to turn it all into syrup, but then I'd have had to store the syrup.  Two things happened while I was accomplishing more important tasks:  The lovely imported sheep's milk feta fell out of the fridge on its head.  The one thing that was just in a plastic vacuform grocery store container full of liquid!  The impact loosened the seal and most of the brine leaked out, which means use it soon.  Yeah, I could have made some kind of brine to refill it but that didn't make as much sense as finding a new job for it when I didn't have all the other ingredients yet. I was thinking cheesecake with the kiwi and feta.  But, while  I've made all kinds of cheesecakes, I'm no expert, and I was thinking eggwhite protein powder instead of wet eggs because of the moisture in the fruit and feta, but I still wasn't sure of the proportions or anything, and I didn't have or find any recipes that would give a good starting point.  Moisture control is at the very center of cooking and baking both, though moreso in baking and especially with a main ingredient that's mostly fat.  ARGH! The other thing that happened?  Petalique had been commending the ginger-pumpkin cheesecake (which she'd posted maybe last year? as a newspaper clipping and which I'd saved), from Mother Wonderful's book (Mother Wonderful's Cheesecakes and Other Goodies: With 20 Absolutely New No-Bake Cheesecakes by Myra Chanin).  Just now, she'd posted it again and shown the book cover as well.  I love books, so I looked it up, and there I found a copy in excellent condition for such an old book.  The other thing that happened was that it arrived! It's an interesting book, but at first I was just seeing recipes very like all the ones I knew.  I needed one for fresh fruit.  I checked the index.  No kiwi :)  No shock.  I looked at orange.  No wet.  Strawberries?  Yes!  A cheesecake recipe with fresh wedges of strawberry mixed in.  That's close.  They even have fairly similar acidity, I think, at least to my tongue.  So, strawberry.  It calls for strawberry liqueur and extract.  I have a jar of Grand Marnier that's going to sugar.  The cork dissolved from old age, so I strained it well, and have been trying to use up the last few ounces.  Orange should go well with kiwi, I thought, and it's not all that orangy.  More boozy and sweet  I omitted the extract in deference to moisture control. For a crust, I'd decided on using up the toasted sliced almonds I'd had left from the roasted apple pie last month, with some cookie crumbs to help hold it together.  I used half the almond slice volume of crumbs.  It could have taken an equal portion, given the air space.  Some of the butter ran out of the spring form for not being absorbed.  BTW, I need too little to put the cookies in the food processor (even the insert small bowl), but didn't want to do the bang with a rolling pin in a plastic bag routine, so I tried putting them through my funky little Chinese hand cranked FP, with the grating blades because I didn't feel kind looking for something \"better\".  It worked just fine.  A little muscle to get it started, then easy sailing to uniform fine crumbs.  I think it worked better than either the rolling pin or the big FP. I read through the commandments of do's and don'ts in the front of the book, some surprising.  I did use the egg protein, moistened with mashed up kiwi instead of water--more kiwi than called for but it was less wet.  It worked fine, but perhaps could have used a third \"egg\".  The kiwi was very sweet, so I cut back the sugar a lot, to maybe a sixth of what was called for, especially so the tang of the feta would be present.  I skipped the salt because of the feta, though.  So, it was half and half by weight, fancy feta (drained on paper of its remaining brine) and Philly, both with plenty of salt by my standards.  And I did the sour cream topping, but my sealed box of sour cream was a little old, and while it wasn't spoiled or moldy or anything, it was very sour, like perhaps trying to ferment?  But it was otherwise perfect, so I just doubled the sugar for that, thinking that the topping didn't need to compete with the feta for tang. So, it came out of the oven lovely and brown on top, but fell a little as I was trying to get the topping on.  I think it could have used a little longer in the oven, or that extra \"egg\".  The center didn't jiggle, but the texture shows where it fell, and is best at the outside where it didn't.  I wasn't going for beauty.  I'd planned to decorate the sides with halves of the red grapes from the kiwi bowl, and to put a few kiwi wedges around the top, but for home use I decided I had better things to do.  :) There are flaws.  I should have hand mixed the cheeses together by hand before beating them.  i had just crumbled the feta and trusted them to marry, during the five minutes of beating with scrapedowns every couple of minutes.  There are occasional pockets of too much tang.  And the kiwi *in* the topping looks lumpy and weird.  I should have just put it on top and made pretty, but I decided it should be cooked along with the topping.  I can't say why.... For all the flaws, this is a really yummy cake, and it doesn't eat heavy like so many of the type do.  I don't know that I'll ever bother to perfect it, but the one I made is well on its way to all gone, and is very enjoyable.", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/8202b1c40757690f_1779-w500-h413-b0-p0--.jpg"]}

title: Home Renovation & Layout Improvement - Which Project to Tackle First? | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "cbeans14", "author_name": "C Beans", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/cbeans14", "date": "2024-12-10", "text": "Hello All - Many of you kindly helped me with a layout dilemma on architectural plans for a home extension a little more than two years ago. So my husband and I are reconsidering the existing layout to see about making the home as comfy and cosy as possible.  Below is the existing layout for the ground floor.  The first floor doesn't need to be touched.   My questions to all of you are as follows: 1. Updating the heating system.  It is currently a vented system with a tank suitable for a 2-bedroom flat and not a 4-bedroom house.  Would you recommend an unvented system or a thermal store (to future-proof the house if we decide to add solar or a heat pump in the future)? 2. If we are updating the heating system, does it make sense to do the wiring (and perhaps CAT-6) as well?  The wiring and fuse box are not old, but it is more about future-proofing. 3. Would it make sense to remove part of the wall between the kitchen and the dining room?  This wall used to be an external wall, so support and steel beams are a must. 4.  What can be done about the conservatory?  It is currently open to the kitchen - there are no doors and therefore on the chilly side.  Adding internal doors is an option, but perhaps there is a better solution. 5. Or is there an option to do something like a glass extension in place of the conservatory?  I came across a product called the SolarLux Wintergarden - I will have to investigate more as I can't see a technical sheet with u-values.  But the idea behind it is that it is warm like a conventional extension but the conservatory's foundation can be used.  The glass extension is supported by the existing house structure plus ground pillars at the corners.  If it is warm like a normal extension - great!  But if it has similar heat loss to our conservatory, it would be a waste of time and money. 6. The kitchen does need a new re-think - it is not a very good layout when there is more than one person in the kitchen. 7. And if you have any other suggestions on the layout, I am all ears. I found several videos about installing the receiver on the unit and controller on the wall, but they are all for the wall mounted units. Mine is a floor mount. There was a red port on the circuit board to plug into, so I opened up my unit and looked at the board.  No port that I could find of any color. If I could find the port, I think I can do this myself for the cost of the part, but I don\u2019t have the skills to change any of the existing components on the board and don\u2019t want to chance damaging anything. other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "outpaientzero", "author_name": "outpaientzero", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/outpaientzero", "date": "2024-12-11", "text": "Moving the thermostat across the room will make the unit run longer, a no brainer. I suggest reading the installation manual for the MHK2 to verify compatibility with your unit. LINK to manual.  http://mylinkdrive.com/USA/Controls/Remote_Controllers/Wall_Mounted_Wireless_MandP/MHK2?product Compatibility is in the applications section with a link to the series you may own, and while you are there look at the other required materials, and note the Kumo cloud app.  In the installation section they state the MHK2 won't work until commissioned through the Kumo cloud app, what ever this means.  The app is said to be free but I also see using the cloud is around $20 a month but I don't know the details. Gah! Please weigh in! I\u2019ve spent a lot of time reading, watching videos, and thinking through how crazy to go with rose winterizing. I made a choice, finished the work, but now am in a major state of self-doubt. The more I read, the more it keeps me up at night. So much conflicting advice. In particular, I\u2019d be really grateful for advice from people with experience in Z6-7 north-eastern US gardens in which winter means on-and-off freezing and a lot of rain or brief snow which then melts ( @KittyNYz6 !) (Please forgive the all-caps / long post -- cringe, haha). MY CURRENT WINTERIZING: I\u2019ve more or less followed Palatine's winterizing approach (e.g., my roses all have 1/2-1 five-gallon bucket\u2019s worth of wood chip mulch poured gently over their crowns and nestled around the first foot or so of growth). With the exception of a very old (bourbon?) rose that lived here long before me, all of my roses are in their first year. The are mostly grafted onto Dr. Huey, but I also have a sprinkling of OR. They are primarily floribundas and hybrid teas with a few outliers. In my garden on the eastern end of our property, I kept the graft union above the soil line because the soil is clay-based and quite poor draining. In my garden to the west, graft unions were planted below the soil line. My concerns: FEEDBACK: I am mostly looking for feedback on whether I should leave my mulch cones or pull the mulch away. Much as I appreciate in-depth, creative solutions for collars, buying fancy mulch varieties, etc. I have too many roses and insufficient funds to pull this off (certainly for this year). I\u2019m still very grateful to hear people\u2019s individual solutions, and might be open to giving a few roses special treatment, but I thought it was worth being up front about my current limitations! MY MICROCLIMATE & SOIL: ZONE: -According to USDA maps, we are literally on the cusp line of 6a/6b. -I think our reality is more like 7a-7b except maybe during occasional harsh winters. We\u2019re on the slope above Cayuga Lake and literally the upper/eastern end of our 8 acres can frost weeks before the lower part, and the field above our property can be covered in snow when we have none, so there\u2019s definitely some microclimate trickery in action! We\u2019ve only lived here two years, so my data is minimal, but I had gladiolus (technically hardy to Z8 but there are reports of them returning in colder zones) and calla lilies (supposedly only hardy to Z8) winter over and reproduce like hotcakes. The giant inherited rose which I think is a bourbon is 7\u2019 tall and suffers zero winter dieback, but has also clearly been established for decades. SOIL: East-side rose garden: rich, clay-based, not well-draining (literally squelchy in the spring). Roses thrived here from bareroot season onward, but other than one old, established bourbon(?), none of them have withstood winter yet. This is the eastern-most end of our property, so it also gets the coldest. West-side rose garden: yard was heavily amended for drainage roughly 15 yrs before we built the house. Has mostly large gravel / coarse rock with newish topsoil. In order to kill off a mega-forest of forsythia, the previous owners chopped down bushes and buried crowns in 4\u2019 of wood chip mulch (local, mixed tree varieties) four years ago. As a result, the roses in this garden are primarily planted in amended soil I carted in which is surrounded by 4\u2019 deep bed of rich, decaying mulch. Overall, this bed tends to run drier and I know the huge amount of mulch in semi-active decay is kicking off heat, which may explain the calla lilies overwintering with glee. First-year roses were fine here in their initial spring, summer, and fall, but definitely preferred the wetter, clay-based eastern garden, where they thrived. WEATHER FACTORS: -Our winters are somewhat wet. We rarely get a true blanket of snow and when we do, it\u2019s thin and usually melts within a few days. -We do have a decent amount of wind, but it mostly harasses the tall trees. i.e., I\u2019m not worried about staking the roses, but leaves wouldn\u2019t work as a mulch\u2014they\u2019d get scooped out of a collar, etc. Okay\u2026. thanks so much for anyone who managed to read all that. I'm all ears!! Tell me what to do!", "images": []}

After some careful planning, we made a freestanding tub work beautifully, all while respecting the existing drain and plumbing locations. By meticulously designing around these constraints, we achieved a space that is functional, stylish, and ready for years of use.    Another significant improvement was the shower. This closet, which housed a water heater in an inconvenient location, was no longer needed after we upgraded to a space-saving tankless water heater. The extra square footage allowed us to create a luxurious, roomy shower. We even added walls to carve out a private toilet room, giving the bathroom a polished and practical layout. The Final Look This project was all about making the most of what we had to work with while infusing each space with style and functionality. title: Kitchen In The Style Of The House | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "jyl-gw", "author_name": "John Liu", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/jyl-gw", "date": "2024-12-13", "text": "In KF, we typically discuss  a  kitchen  all on its own.  Maybe the OP includes a bit of the adjoining room.  Almost never, when musing about quartzite or Taj Mahal, apron front or workstation, white shaker or slab veneer, do we know if the house has a specific architectural style. Often, houses don't have a specific architectural style.  They are blank canvases.  But some houses, older ones, do have a strong identity, are of an era, with the characteristics and details of a 1890 Queen Anne, a 1905 Craftsman bungalow, a 1940 Tudor Revival, a 1935 Spanish Colonial Revival, a 1928 French Revival, an 1930 Art Deco/Moderne. I like to think that we\u2019d be told if this were the case.  I'd hate to think we were part of discarding that Queen Anne's original details and bead-board wainscoting for slab veneer-on-MDF doors and walls slathered with Taj Mahal. But maybe we were.  The mainstream kitchen industry has a set of standard looks, that change every decade or so, and it is so much easier to adopt one of those, than to build the curves of a Deco, the texture and details of a Tudor, the mass and solid wood of a Craftsman, or the characteristics of other historical styles. And so you walk into that Queen Anne and find a 2020s Standard Kitchen.  A lovely one, beautifully designed, worthy of ooos and aahs in isolation.  But in that house, it looks wrong and uncaring. The poor MCM house suffers too.  Its cabinets are too grainy , counters too colorful, appliances too old fashioned - give it white Shaker and subway tiles, we nod, having no idea what the house looks like beyond that room. So . . . title: Basic Workout Routine on a Compact Exercise Bike | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "relife-sports-pfvwus-pf~944447487", "author_name": "Relife sports", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/home-stagers/relife-sports-pfvwus-pf~944447487", "date": "2024-12-13", "text": "A compact exercise bike is a smaller, space-saving version of a traditional stationary bike, designed for home use or limited spaces. These bikes are ideal for people who want a low-impact cardio workout but have limited space in their homes or apartments. They typically offer the same features as full-sized bikes but with a more compact and portable design. Key Features of Compact Exercise Bike Space-Saving Design: Smaller footprint, often foldable or with adjustable handlebars and seats for easy storage. Adjustable Resistance: Similar to regular exercise bikes, they allow you to adjust the difficulty of your workout by increasing or decreasing the resistance. Comfort: Some compact bikes come with padded seats or ergonomic designs to ensure comfort during workouts. Digital Display: Many models have a built-in console that tracks time, distance, speed, calories burned, and other fitness metrics. Quiet Operation: Most compact exercise bikes use magnetic resistance or belt-driven systems, making them quieter than traditional friction-based systems. Portability: Many are lightweight and come with wheels for easy movement. Types of Compact Exercise Bike Mini Exercise Bikes: Pedal-only bikes are often used at a desk or on a chair. They\u2019re great for low-impact exercise and can be used for upper and lower-body workouts. Foldable Exercise Bikes: Full-sized stationary bikes that can be folded for storage. They offer a more complete workout experience than mini bikes, with adjustable handlebars and resistance. Benefits of compact exercise bike Convenient: Great for people with limited time or space. Low-Impact: Ideal for users with joint issues or beginners. Affordable: Generally more affordable than larger, full-featured exercise bikes. These bikes can be found at a wide range of prices depending on features and build quality. Using a compact exercise bike provides an excellent low-impact workout that improves cardiovascular health, burns calories, and strengthens muscles. Here's a comprehensive workout routine you can do on a compact exercise bike, whether it's a pedal-only version or a full-sized, foldable stationary bike. Basic Workout Routine on a Compact Exercise Bike 1. Warm-Up (5\u201310 minutes) Start at a low resistance to gently get your body moving. Pedal at a comfortable pace (easy to moderate effort). If using a mini exercise bike, simply pedal with your legs or even add upper-body movements if you have a seated version. 2. Steady-State Cardio (15\u201325 minutes) Set a moderate resistance level that allows you to pedal at a consistent pace. Maintain a steady pace that you can sustain for the entire duration without feeling exhausted. Focus on breathing deeply and evenly as you cycle. Aim for a target heart rate in the moderate range (about 50-70% of your maximum heart rate). 3. Interval Training (10\u201320 minutes) This workout alternates between high-intensity efforts and low-intensity recovery periods. High-Intensity Phase (1\u20132 minutes): Increase the resistance or pedal as fast as you can, reaching 80-90% of your maximum effort. Recovery Phase (1\u20132 minutes): Lower the resistance or slow your pace to allow your heart rate to recover. Repeat the cycle for 10\u201320 minutes. For example, after 1 minute of intense pedaling, follow it with 1 minute of slower, more relaxed pedaling. Interval training helps burn more calories and improves cardiovascular fitness in less time than steady-state cardio. 4. Endurance Ride (20\u201330 minutes) If you're focusing on building stamina, try pedaling at a moderate pace for 20-30 minutes at a consistent level of resistance. This is a steady, long-duration ride aimed at improving aerobic fitness. Avoid excessively high resistance to keep the pace steady. 5. Cool Down (5\u201310 minutes) Gradually reduce the intensity of your pedaling and let your heart rate slowly return to its resting state. Pedal at a very low resistance, focusing on deep, controlled breathing. If you\u2019re using a mini bike, focus on gentle pedal strokes to relax the muscles.", "images": []}

title: Retrofit vs Brick to Brick Question | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "sarah-t97", "author_name": "Sarah T", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/sarah-t97", "date": "2024-12-14", "text": "I'm getting new windows and decided to do brick to brick installation because I want to make sure the wood is ok and have it done properly. There is a company that has an aluminum/vinyl clad window I like but this was their response about doing 'brick to brick'. I would love to hear if anyone has any advice on this. (My house is 2x4 construction) \"yesterday we have discussed your project with our technicians going through the pictures. This may be a tricky installation because we don\u2019t exactly know whats hidden behind the aluminum exterior cappings, all being different sizes, jambs missing or having different depths \u2013 so other option to supply and install windows for your house would be to use H3 Transcend Replacement Retrofit. This is exactly the same product as regular H3 except it doesn\u2019t come with jamb extensions and can be installed without removing your existing casings and jambs, so installers avoid running into issues related with removal of existing jambs and casings on the interior.\" \"This is an older house with virtually no jamb extensions because there\u2019s no room for it. Some of ones that you currently have, have different depths. Also some exterior aluminum caps are different sizes overlapping windows in different capacity and we just don\u2019t know what\u2019s behind it, if there\u2019s any structural detail, if there\u2019s a reason they were installed like that.With going retrofit we would at least cross out one of the problems and leave the existing interior\"", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/8e8288e9075ce1cc_0419-w500-h1082-b0-p0--.jpg"]}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "pfvwus-pf~756118809", "author_name": "Windows on Washington Ltd", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/pfvwus-pf~756118809", "date": "2024-12-14", "text": "Can you post up a picture or two?  If the primary driver isn't total glass (i.e. frame size) area, and the retrofit was working before, there is nothing to say that it won't continue to work. Are the current, possibly retrofit, windows capped as well?  When we tear out a retrofit and capped window, we inspect all the wood that is under the capping (sill, old frame, trim, etc.).  Most times, assuming the previous window was done properly, the wood is fine and drier that it ever way.  Re-capping as part of the new window ensures that bulk moisture transfer to the wood is eliminated and all you are dealing with is some capillary draw which normally won't present as an issue. Do you have an evidence of any leaks?  I suppose you could remove some of the capping on one window and inspect the wood beneath, but that is rarely done unless there is some history of leaks and the contractor is trying to get a handle of the scope so that the change orders aren't as significant. I don't see anything in the prior commentary from the contractor as a red flag.  Often times its more about correlating the verbiage of what the installer/contractor is seeing and thinking to what the homeowner is understanding.  When you get into exterior trim removal, rough opening sizes, brick openings, drainage planes, etc., it can be hard for the contractor to effectively relate what they are saying.  I find that it is always easiest on the job site and maybe with some selective demo of the trim/opening to demonstrate.", "images": []}}

title: "American Symphony" | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "sushipup2", "author_name": "sushipup2", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/sushipup2", "date": "2024-12-17", "text": "We just watched \"American Symphony\" the documentary about Jon Batiste and his wife Suleika Jaouad.  It's a story about music and love.  A wonderful love story.  Filmed while Jon was up for 11 Grammies, winning 5, while Suleika was undergoing a bone marrow transplant for the recurrence of her leukemia.  All the while he is writing the symphony and preparing for Carnegie Hall. A beautiful beautiful movie.  It's on Netflix, and I recommend it.", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "mtnrdredux-gw", "author_name": "mtnrdredux_gw", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/mtnrdredux-gw", "date": "2024-12-17", "text": "These words, from Suleika, are really profound for all of us: For the last few months, small joys have been my sustenance\u2026 Often these small moments fade from view with the passage of time. What makes it into our memory banks are the bigger things\u2014either the zeniths or the nadirs\u2014but what we end up longing for and leaning on in hard times are the little quotidian comforts and delights; they lift and carry us from day to day. Noting these joys is a muscle I\u2019ve been consciously trying to exercise: training the eye to see them and training the mind to hold onto them. I do want to make a distinction here between the practice of celebrating small joys and the culture of \u201ctoxic positivity,\u201d where we\u2019re told to be ever-grateful, to always search for the silver linings, to put a positive spin on all experiences, even the profoundly tragic. The author Barbara Ehrenreich has written critically about this cultural phenomenon with far more nuance than I can in this missive, but it\u2019s a topic I\u2019ve thought a lot about, especially in these last months. It\u2019s easy to feel pressure to be someone who \u201csuffers well\u201d\u2014grateful and graceful and stoic 24/7. But that doesn\u2019t allow us to exist fully, to experience the full range of the human condition, from happiness to grief, from gratitude to envy. I love observing tiny daily joys because it feels natural and easy, not forced, not pressurized, not all or nothing. And not only has the practice helped ease this difficult passage, it\u2019s helped me identify what lifts me up, and then I can cultivate more of it. I also think this, below is something many people could benefit from as a \"policy.\" A Few Requests & Ways to Help\u2014 In sharing this news with the community, I\u2019d also like to include a few of the same requests that I sent two years ago when I wrote about my relapse. Please no pity, no advice, no unsolicited medical information, no dietary recommendations, no alternative cures from your great-grandmother\u2019s guru. I appreciate the good intentions behind these impulses, but please know that (unfortunately) I have a lot of experience when it comes to cancer, and I\u2019m choosing the right path for me. What I do invite is love. I\u2019ve been the very fortunate recipient of so much loving care. Yet there are many out there who are not so fortunate\u2014and some of them are people in your own life. Konkret geht es dabei um die Trauf- und Firsth\u00f6he, die wir in Bezug auf einen Referenzpunkt (336,02m \u00fc. NN) \u00fcberschreiten. Absolut gesehen haben wir TH und FH mit 6,4m bzw. 10,45m zwar eingehalten (Vorgabe: 6,5m bzw. 10,5m), der Referenzpunkt liegt aber quasi unterhalb der Bodenplatte, weswegen wir TH und FH um etwa 50cm \u00fcberschreiten. Bei anderen H\u00e4usern im Baugebiet wurden wohl etwa 20cm toleriert, aber da sind wir nat\u00fcrlich deutlich dr\u00fcber. Im Umkehrschluss bedeutet dies nun, dass unser Kniestock auf 0 geht und das Dachgeschoss um etwa 30cm abgesenkt werden muss. Damit sind Hobbyraum und Dachspitz nicht mehr sinnvoll nutzbar und auch das Bad b\u00fc\u00dft einiges ein. Um den fehlenden Platz zu kompensieren hatten wir nun \u00fcberlegt, statt einer Bodenplatte doch einen Keller zu bauen. H\u00e4tte nebenbei auch den Vorteil, dass wir keine Brunnengr\u00fcndung unterhalb der Bodenplatte mehr ben\u00f6tigen w\u00fcrden (Nachbar besitzt einen Keller, n\u00f6tig zur Lastabtragung) und wir k\u00f6nnten uns Dachspitz und Dachfenster sparen. W\u00e4re in Summe trotzdem deutlich teurer, aber wir h\u00e4tten wenigstens einen Mehrwert durch den Keller. Ein Keller w\u00fcrde nat\u00fcrlich auch gewisse Ver\u00e4nderungen im Grundriss mit sich bringen - v.a. im Erdgeschoss (Technikraum aus dem EG und Hobbyraum aus dem DG w\u00fcrden dann in den Keller wandern). Daher nun die Frage an euch, wie ihr mit dem gewonnenen Raum umgehen w\u00fcrdet. Am Grundriss der K\u00fcche mit Zeile, Insel und Nische w\u00fcrden wir gerne festhalten, wie auch an der Aufteilung im OG. Im DG ist uns nur wichtig, dass Schlafzimmer und Bad Platz finden. Grunds\u00e4tzlich sind wir aber f\u00fcr alle Vorschl\u00e4ge offen bzw. gerne auch f\u00fcr Hinweise, falls uns Planungsfehler unterlaufen sind oder R\u00e4ume ggf. (wegen der Gr\u00f6\u00dfe z.B.) nur schlecht nutzbar sind. Gleiches gilt auch f\u00fcr Ideen, wie wir den jetzigen Grundriss \"retten\" k\u00f6nnen. That was maybe 6 weeks ago, and over the past week or two it has started refusing to open again. We could still get it to open after a few tries but we were thinking we will probably have to replace this stupid thing. Well, this morning my bowl of oatmeal got stuck and I can NOT get the door open. My oatmeal is in prison. title: The Power of Visual Storytelling in the Digital Age | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "khurram-shahzad143", "author_name": "khurram shahzad", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/khurram-shahzad143", "date": "2024-12-22", "text": "In today\u2019s fast-paced, content-driven world, grabbing and holding your audience\u2019s attention has become a fine art. With countless pieces of information vying for eyes and clicks, storytelling has emerged as a critical strategy for making a brand or message stand out. And when paired with visuals, storytelling transforms into a force to be reckoned with. Visuals have a unique ability to simplify complex concepts, evoke emotions, and create lasting impressions. Whether through graphics, videos, or even innovative text to image solutions, visuals breathe life into narratives, making them more engaging and impactful. But how do you harness this power effectively? Visuals: Beyond Aesthetic Appeal It\u2019s a common misconception that visuals are merely decorative. While aesthetics are important, the true power of visuals lies in their ability to convey messages faster and more effectively than text alone. Consider infographics, for example. A well-designed infographic can communicate complex data in seconds, making it a preferred medium for professionals and casual readers alike. Another example is branded imagery on social media. A picture tailored to align with your brand\u2019s voice and ethos can evoke a sense of connection and trust. Such imagery can make your brand\u2019s story stick in your audience\u2019s mind long after they\u2019ve scrolled past it. Storytelling with a Twist Traditional storytelling has its merits, but the digital landscape calls for more dynamic approaches. Enter interactive visuals. Tools like carousels, clickable graphics, and creative design elements offer users a participatory experience, turning them from passive readers into active participants. This twist keeps users engaged longer and fosters a stronger connection to the content. Moreover, the evolution of technology has made it easier than ever to create bespoke visuals. Online tools allow even non-designers to craft professional-grade graphics tailored to their needs. From creating simple memes to crafting intricate designs, the possibilities are endless. The Future of Visual Storytelling As storytelling continues to evolve, the visual landscape is bound to expand. Imagine personalized visuals that adapt to different themes or handcrafted graphics that align seamlessly with your brand\u2019s tone. The potential for innovation in this space is immense. One thing is certain: visuals will remain a cornerstone of effective communication. By investing in the right tools and strategies, brands and creators can stay ahead of the curve and continue to captivate their audiences. In conclusion, the fusion of storytelling and visuals is not just a passing trend; it\u2019s a fundamental shift in how we communicate. So, whether you\u2019re crafting a marketing campaign, sharing a personal project, or simply telling a story, let visuals do the heavy lifting. After all, a picture is worth a thousand words, and in the digital age, it might just be worth a thousand clicks too.", "images": []}

title: Types of Exercise Bikes for Home | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "relife-sports-pfvwus-pf~944447487", "author_name": "Relife sports", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/home-stagers/relife-sports-pfvwus-pf~944447487", "date": "2024-12-24", "text": "An exercise bike for home is a great way to incorporate cardiovascular exercise into your routine, especially if you prefer working out at home. When choosing an exercise bike, there are several factors to consider, such as type, features, and budget. Types of Exercise Bikes for Home A. Upright Bikes Description: The most traditional type of exercise bike for home, similar to a road bike, where you sit upright and pedal. Best For: General cardio, weight loss, and lower body toning. Features to Look For: Adjustable seat and handlebars for comfort. Varying resistance levels for different intensity levels. Compact design, ideal for small spaces. B. Recumbent Bikes Description: These exercise bikes for home have a larger seat and back support, allowing you to recline while you pedal. The pedals are positioned in front of you, not below. Best For: People with back or joint issues, seniors, or those seeking a more comfortable workout. Features to Look For: Comfortable, adjustable seating with backrest. Easy to get on and off. They are more stable than upright bikes, making them ideal for those with balance concerns. C. Spin Bikes (Indoor Cycling) Description: These are designed for more intense workouts and mimic the feel of riding a road bike. They have a heavy flywheel and are built for vigorous cycling workouts. Best For: People looking for a high-intensity workout, especially those interested in spin classes or HIIT cycling. Features to Look For: Adjustable resistance for interval training. Large flywheel for smooth motion. Adjustable seat and handlebars. D. Air Bikes Description: Air bikes use a fan for resistance, which increases as you pedal harder. These bikes provide a full-body workout since they also have moving handlebars. Best For: High-intensity interval training (HIIT) and those looking for a challenging full-body workout. Features to Look For: Air resistance for scalable difficulty. Moving handlebars to engage the upper body. Durable construction for intense workouts. Features to Consider Resistance System: Magnetic Resistance: Quiet and smooth, often found in upright and recumbent bikes. Fan/ Air Resistance: Found in air bikes, offering resistance that increases the harder you pedal. Friction Resistance: A more traditional system, often used in spin bikes. Adjustability: Look for a bike with adjustable seats and handlebars to ensure proper posture and comfort during your workout. title: Speaking of blow mold Santas..... | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "pudgeder", "author_name": "pudgeder", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/pudgeder", "date": "2024-12-25", "text": "The year my husband & I bought our 1st home, we bought a blow-mold 5.5 foot Santa from Sears. It was our 1st (and only) outside Christmas decoration. Years later, we had moved to another house in a small town. The neighborhood was always decorated lavishly for the holidays. It was so pretty! We had Santa for many years, gradually adding lights, on the house, lining the sidewalk & curb,  and the kids always looked forward to putting Santa outside. He was the last thing we put up and we did it together. (well, usually.) My oldest son would have been in junior high, which would have made Santa about 15+ yrs old. So for 15 years, we had the tradition of putting up this plastic Santa in the yard.   DH would strap him to a tree in the front yard so he wouldn't fall over or blow away. Usually 2 ratchet straps held St. Nick in place. Until one year...... someone stole Santa. And his tethers. They didn't vandalize any of the lights or other decor in the yard. Just stole our beloved plastic blow mold Santa. Darling daughter, 9, was so distraught. How could anyone steal our decorations?   We just chalked it up as lesson learned, and never put any thing other than lights up from then on. 3 years later on Christmas eve, Santa returned. Ratchet straps & all. He wasn't strapped to the tree, but standing on the porch. Oh, and they plugged him in, so he was lit up! No explanation, no ring the door bell & run, just  **poof** he was back! We've moved again since then, and sadly, Santa got smooshed and was never quite the same. But he must have had some adventure when he was AWOL for 3 years! LOL", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "bpath", "author_name": "bpath", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/bpath", "date": "2024-12-25", "text": "I wonder if there is a \u201dwandering Santa\u201d. In our old neighborhood, there was a Santa roaming around in the late fall. He started out kind of toppled over by the creek, then he was on the slide in the tot lot, then atop the fort, then on the sidewalk down the block, then he ended up in my neighbor\u2019s yard. She asked if we wanted him as they didn\u2019t observe Christmas, so we took him in, got him a light bulb, and set him up in front of the house. DH didn\u2019t like him at all, but I put him up (Santa, that is) for a few years. One night I was up with the baby, about 11pm. I heard a kind of a bang, then giggling, a car door slamming, and was to the window in time to see a car drive off. Yep, it was a hit man. Probably with a baseball bat. The light bulb broke, Santa had ben sent sprawling on the lawn (at least as far as the cord let it). I joking accused DH of hiring a hit man. Santa got donated a year later.", "images": []}}

title: Interior design visualization | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "webuser-150734210", "author_name": "HU-150734210", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/webuser-150734210", "date": "2024-12-26", "text": "Establishing Solid Relationships with Vendors and Clients Through Interior Design Visualization In the field of interior design, success depends mostly on building close relationships. This covers the relationships developed with reliable suppliers in addition to the link between designers and their clients. Transposing design ideas into reality depends on these suppliers, who range in their offerings from furniture to fixtures. Good relationships with these vendors not only enable interior designers to produce perfect designs but also increase vendor sales and brand recognition. Conversely, customers want flawless project performance with little disturbance and excellent output. How therefore may interior designers improve relationships with vendors as well as their clients? The secret is the effective instrument of interior design visualizing. Why Effective Teams Depend on Interior Design Visualization? Showing their products in realistic environments\u2014often using 3D renderings\u2014one of the main ways vendors interact with possible customers. Designers also employ 3D models to vividly realize their ideas for clients. This common use of 3D rendering tools bridges the designer, the vendor, and the client. It improves the communication process and fosters enduring, effective partnerships as well. Interior design visualization helps to establish confidence and enhance cooperation among all the stakeholders by means of its effects. First step: getting 3D models from vendors. New, creative ideas to include into their designs are constantly sought for by interior designers. Whether they are looking through internet sites, visiting trade exhibitions, or perusing showrooms, they get ideas from a broad spectrum. Designers must discover means to include objects they adore into their creations. Here is where visualizing of interior design is quite important. Requesting 3D models or digital prototypes from manufacturers helps designers make sure the objects they wish to include in their projects are faithfully shown in their visualizations. Alternatively, to produce models based on product photos and specifications, designers might commission 3D rendering services from a professional studio. This procedure not only saves time but also builds a good working relationship with the vendors, who would value the designer's intention to use and advertise their products in next projects. The second step is visualizing interior design using 3D models. Once designers have 3D models of the goods they wish to feature, they can forward them to a CGI company for rendering. Detailed interior renderings depicting clients exactly how their space will look once the project is finished are created from these 3D models. For the visualization studio, using already-existing 3D models of furniture, appliances, and decor greatly lessens the effort. The method is quicker and less expensive since artists do not have to make fresh, from- scratch objects. The designer, who depends on reliable suppliers for premium models, gets from this simplified process; the vendor receives visibility via the designer's projects. Moreover, clients' confidence in the design increases when they view reasonable depictions of their future environments with real objects. They are aware that the end product will quite mirror the 3D renderings, so minimizing any shocks or future uncertainty. Making clients a ready-made shopping list in step three Working with 3D rendering services is one of the main benefits in that it lets clients have a complete shopping list. Clients can quickly determine what they need to buy from the 3D drawings, therefore saving time and effort in item sourcing by means of actual product identification. Digital visuals also facilitate budget control. Clients can evaluate whether the things shown in the renders fit their budget by reviewing their pricing. Should it be necessary, changes can be done and more reasonably priced substitutes can be recommended to make sure the project stays within budgetary constraints while still having aesthetic value. Fourth step: quick changes using interior design visualization Using interior design visualization also helps one to appreciate the simplicity of design modification possible. Designers may rapidly replace elements utilizing 3D models from their library whether a client wants changes to the design, for budgetary or aesthetic reasons. Since the additional components can be included into already-existing scenarios, this reduces the necessity for starting from nothing. Presenting fresh visuals right away guarantees that consumers are always in the loop and can fast accept the modifications. Moreover, the availability of actual product prices facilitates the evaluation of whether the new products fall inside the customer's means. Storing 3D models for further projects comes in step five. Designers can retain the 3D models and digital resources for usage in next projects once a current one is finished. Working with a 3D rendering services provider frequently means designers may have their models kept in a safe, orderly database for simple access as needed. The designer can easily draw from their current collection of assets, therefore eliminating the need to reimagine the wheel for every new project. Because the designer may recycle known items and resources, this not only saves time but guarantees consistency between projects. Working with a visualization studio to save these assets also guarantees correct organization and easy access to the files, therefore reducing the possibility of losing priceless resources. In essence, improving relationships with 3D rendering services As you can see, interior design visualization is far more than simply a creative tool; it's a potent means of developing confidence and strengthening ties with vendors and customers. Interior designers may enhance communication, simplify project management, and finally provide a better experience for all those engaged by using 3D rendering technologies to produce realistic visualizations. Interior design visualization benefits designers, suppliers, and consumers equally whether it's for product showcases, correct budgets, or speedy design modifications.", "images": []}

Went out with a girlfriend, stopped on the way home at the grocery store for a few things. As a former hairdresser, I was very hair aware and noticed the cashier's beautiful hair and great haircut. Wrote a check for groceries and left with my friend. Several days later, I got a letter in my mailbox...it was from that cashier who told me that he was my son and had JUST that same day gotten my current address. He was raised in Olympia. Il costruttore mi ha proposto una sua idea di planimetria, lasciandoci carta bianca su eventuali modifiche alle disposizioni, con unici vincoli nella posizione e dimensione delle finestre, nonch\u00e9 nelle colonne portanti che non possono essere spostate. Abbiamo fatto qualche modifica alla planimetria iniziale, arrivando alla soluzione che trovate qui in foto. Non essendo esperti, ci farebbe piacere ricevere qualche consiglio, in modo da arrivare con le idee un po' pi\u00f9 chiare nel momento in cui ci rivolgeremo ad un professionista. Vi do alcune caratteristiche di base dell'immobile: - metratura interna calpestabile (esclusi quindi i terrazzi), circa 116 mq - posizionamento al secondo ed ultimo piano - orientamento (guardando la foto che vi allego) nord (zona notte+bagni)-est-sud(zona giorno) - vi ho evidenziato in giallo il vano scale che non fa parte dell'appartamento La nostra premura principale sarebbe quella di avere una zona giorno ampia e funzionale, \"sacrificando\" eventualmente qualcosina nella zona notte. I dubbi principali che abbiamo sono: - disposizione degli arredi, soprattutto nei due bagni - aprire o meno la cucina, creando un open space - ridurre il disimpegno, che al momento pensavamo in realt\u00e0 di sfruttare come zona armadio di servizio (per giacconi ed altre cose da non riporre nelle camere), oltre che per i passaggi delle canalizzazioni a soffitto Le metrature delle stanze ci sembrano abbastanza congrue, ma se avete suggerimenti sono ben accetti. Unico vincolo \u00e8 quello di avere le 3 camere, in quanto l'appartamento sar\u00e0 al momento abitato da 2 persone, ma con previsione di estensione a 4. All of Louisa May Alcott (I grew up in the same town as that author), Rosemary Sutcliffe (who influenced my life-long love of England), and many of the Newbery Medal winners (and Caldecott ones as well).
